blocks.md: This lesson follows **Fallacies and Pitfalls** in *Closed-Loop Evaluation* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Closed-Loop Evaluation, § Fallacies and Pitfalls
blocks.md: An empirical evaluation supports engineering claims only within the precise physical boundaries and statistical assumptions of its test protocol. In embodied machine learning systems, severe evaluation errors arise when teams extrapolate localized results across untested operational envelopes or attribute system-level safety guarantees to a learned policy when deterministic enforcement mechanisms actually did the work.

questions.q: The section **Fallacies and Pitfalls** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Coverage gaps the record cannot close become five runtime monitor channels (input support, latency and freshness, constraint margin, intervention rate, environmental assumption).

Replay, closed-loop simulation, shadow operation, and constrained physical testing sit on two axes (causal feedback, physical realism) and each trades one distortion for another, so they are not a fidelity ladder.

At zero failures the Wald interval collapses, so a clean record is inverted exactly (failure bound about 3/n), which makes twenty clean runs consistent with a one-in-seven failure rate and makes every added nine cost about ten times the trials.

Shadow operation runs the candidate on the real machine while the baseline keeps authority, so the candidate's inputs stay confined to the baseline's state distribution and its recovery is never tested.
